transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-12
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Sofia Ruiz (Redwood Solutions Eng); Lena Ortiz (Oakmoss CTO), Tom Brooks (Oakmoss SRE Lead), Ravi Menon (Oakmoss Platform), Priya Shah (Oakmoss PM)

[00:00] Maya: okay everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off. quick intro from redwood side — maya ae, arjun se, sofia solutions. and oakmoss?
[00:12] Lena: hi yeah lena here, quick context — we're building a customer support assistant and an embeddings search pipeline. main asks: p95 latency for streaming chat under 350ms, and embeddings throughput at ~4000 docs / min, curious about hosted vs dedicated costs.
[00:30] Arjun: awesome, that helps. two quick clarifying q's — what's your average prompt len and target model family (so we can scope tokens/sec)?
[00:40] Tom: for chat mostly short prompts, 20-60 tokens in the prompt, responses ~50 tokens typical. embeddings are 512-d vectors per doc, doc sizes vary but avg 800 tokens pre-chunking.
[00:55] Maya: great. so for streaming p95 under 350ms that depends on model, sequence len, and whether you're on hosted with our pooled infra or dedicated reserved GPUs. rough ballpark: hosted small models with continuous batching can hit p95 sub-300ms for 8k context models for short responses; larger models it's trickier.
[01:20] Ravi: can you unpack continuous batching — we have bursty traffic, sometimes 200 concurrent users, sometimes 10. how do you handle that without spiking latency?
[01:30] Arjun: yeah so continuous batching groups inflight requests into micro-batches to improve GPU util; we also do adaptive batching — if latency SLO tight we reduce batch windows and fall back to lower-cost pathways. for bursts we route by policy: reserved dedicated pool first, then hosted burst, and private if provisioned.
[01:50] Priya: are there hard numbers on tokens/sec per GPU for the models you're recommending? we need that to capacity-plan.
[01:58] Arjun: sure, on an A100-like node for a 13B quantized float16 variant we're seeing about 400-800 tokens/sec for generation at steady-state w/ KV cache warm; for 7B it's roughly 1200–2000 tokens/sec. but these numbers are noisy — depends on seq len and streaming overhead.
[02:20] Tom: okay, for our chat flow we care about p95 per token emission as well — streaming latency is the sum of network + server + decode overhead. do you do prefix caching? we've got a lot of repeated utterances.
[02:34] Sofia: yes we do prefix / KV caching — if you have repeated system prompts or instruction prefixes that reduces decode compute a lot. helpful for you since many prompts share a common system template.
[02:46] Lena: data residency — we need audit logs, KMS, and want private deployment in our EU region ideally. SOC2 required. what's the path?
[02:56] Maya: standard path is hosted eval -> dedicated reserved if you need predictability -> private (VPC) for data residency. for private we ship a customer-managed control plane and integrate with your KMS/HSM. we have SOC2 docs, and we can provide deployment checklist. we'll send that.
[03:12] Tom: any differences in p95 when on private vs hosted? our infra team is worried private might add network egress or cold-start overhead
[03:22] Arjun: good q — private adds minimal extra latency if deployed in the same region and with proper networking. main delta is environment variability — you control autoscaler config; if your cluster is underprovisioned you'll see higher tail latencies. we recommend a small reserved buffer and warm-up probes for KV cache.
[03:40] Priya: cost — if we pick dedicated, what's cost delta vs hosted per token?
[03:47] Maya: it depends on commit size. rough numbers: hosted per-token includes infra + multi-tenant premium; dedicated is lower per-token at scale but requires monthly commitment. we'll send a sample SKU sheet.
[03:58] Ravi: we also want to run a benchmark — p95 under synthetic and real traffic. what does your benchmark template look like?
[04:05] Arjun: we have a benchmark workbook — includes traffic profile generator, seq_len distributions, concurrency ramps, and telemetry hooks for p95, p50, coldstart rate, token/sec, and GPU util. we'll share a Google sheet and a small runner harness (lightweight) you can run in your VPC or against hosted endpoints.
[04:26] Lena: can you run a hosted pilot first? we want a 48-hour run with our typical traffic shape. also, we want to validate edge cases — token storms and mid-day bursts.
[04:36] Maya: yep we can do a hosted pilot. typical approach: 1) run synthetic baseline ramp 2) run a replay of your historical trace (if you can share) 3) capture p95 and token/sec under load. after that we iterate on batching and quant.
[04:50] Tom: about quantization — how safe is it for our LLM outputs? we can't have hallucinations increase.
[04:58] Arjun: understood. we recommend stepwise evaluation — int8 / quant settings that maintain accuracy vs float16. Redwood Optimize gives quality regression alerts tied to your eval prompts. we'll include recommended prompt suites to watch for regressions.
[05:12] Priya: what about concurrency multiplexing — we want to keep many short streams open (like 600 concurrent websockets). can you support that?
[05:21] Arjun: yes, our runtime supports multiplexing across connections. the limiting factor is total simultaneous decode tokens/sec and memory for KV caches. for 600 short streams you'll need to size nodes for concurrency rather than pure token throughput. we can provide a sizing matrix — we'll include that in the follow-up.
[05:40] Lena: any compliance gotchas — SSO, RBAC, audit logs?
[05:44] Maya: we support SAML/SSO integrations, role-based access, and long-term audit retention as an add-on. for private deployments logs can be pushed to your SIEM.
[05:55] Ravi: ok, last technical — fallback behavior: if a model variant or dedicated pool is saturated, how do you route?
[06:03] Arjun: routing policies let you fallback to a cheaper smaller model or to a lower-cost region with graded degradation. we can configure per-route fallbacks with canary percentages to avoid sudden regressions.
[06:14] Tom: perfect. want to confirm the pilot access — we'll need an API key scoped to a test project, and a template for the VPC peering if we go private.
[06:23] Maya: we'll send the pilot onboarding doc and API key provisioning steps.
[06:28] -- meeting continues with deeper probing about seq_len distributions and specifics --
[20:10] Arjun: (notes) for Oakmoss chat: target p95 350ms for first token emit; recommended starting config: dedicated 2x A100 nodes for warm KV cache + hosted burst. concurrency target: 600 ws connections, estimated sustained tokens/sec 6k for peak, embeddings pipeline 4000 docs/min on 4x GPU batch workers.
[20:36] Lena: those numbers sound reasonable, want to validate with pilot.
[20:40] Maya: next steps recap — we'll share bench sheet, quant/quality notes, SOC2 & VPC checklist, propose pilot times. set up pilot run week of 9/20.
[20:55] Priya: ok schedule invite, and Tom will provision test infra. thanks all.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-asr missed a few proper nouns and swapped 'quantization' with 'quantize nation' in places. occasional speaker mismatch around 00:40-01:00.
